blocks.x: Both are reserved ahead of every word ([reserved strokes](#/ref/reserved-strokes)). The modifier dictionary is generated by lyk's own `modifier-chords.py` and follows the community's "Emily's modifier chords" scheme (Plover fingerspelling plus a chorded Ctrl/Alt/Super/Shift ending), so existing muscle memory carries over; independent of the theory.
The alphabet
Each letter is one chord, the same as the starting sounds (`PW` b, `TK` d, `STKPW` z). Columns: bare chord, glued form, glued capital, Shift+letter stroke.
*y* is `KWR*` glued but `KWH` in the modifier dictionary and [spelling mode](#/ref/spelling-mode). Every other letter has the same chord in all three.
`LGTS` strokes with a vowel-only chord have no hyphen: `A`, `E`, `U`, `EU` are written `AFLGTS`, `EFLGTS`, `UFLGTS`, `EUFLGTS`. Chords ending in a consonant key need it: `S-FLGTS`, `KR-FLGTS`.
Fingerspelling in running text
Letter chord plus `*` glues the letter to adjacent letters only. Add `-P` for a capital. Both are first-up with `*` exempt (below).

Hold the star, tap letters

Every glued letter entry starts with `{:firstup:except=*}`: `A*` is `{:firstup:except=*}{>}{&a}`, `A*P` is `{:firstup:except=*}{&A}`. Hold `*` and tap letter chords: each tap is one letter ([[T*]] [[A*]] [[KR*]] write t, a, c with `*` held throughout).

items: All 52 strokes carry the marker, lowercase and capital. No other entry in `punctuation.json` does, and none of the 52 is a modifier chord or command stroke, so a held `*` never turns into another family: modifier chords need `LGTS` and exempt `-FRPBLGTS`, the cursor family needs `STPH`.
A letter stroke always has a letter key besides `*`; `*` alone stays [undo](#/ref/punctuation), on its last key up, and no stroke of only exempt keys carries the marker.
Only these entries are first-up. A dictionary word that shares a chord with a letter (the bare chord, no `*`) is unaffected.

**Downside.** A letter chord of several keys (`TK` d, `KW` q, `PH` m) now goes when the first of its keys comes up. Lifting one key of the chord early sends a smaller stroke, and the key still down joins the next stroke. Land the keys of a chord together.
Needs a keymux build that reads `{:firstup:except=KEYS}`; see [Send on the first key up](#/ref/punctuation/send-on-the-first-key-up). Plain Plover errors on the marker.

blocks.x: Not ported from Plover: the number-bar chords, the `-RBGS` forms, and the trailing-hyphen or trailing-period forms.
A word with no outline (see [briefs](#/ref/briefs)) is costed as one stroke per letter.

Modifier chords: the LGTS dictionary
Every stroke:
[chord for the key] + [modifier keys on the right hand] + LGTS

items: The ender `LGTS` (right hand's bottom four keys, `-LGTS`) is on all 1,470 strokes; it keeps ordinary outlines from colliding with modifier chords.
At least one modifier key must be held; a bare letter or symbol is not this dictionary's job.
Output is wrapped in `{^}` on both sides: attaches to nothing, adds no space.

**First-up.** Every entry starts with `{:firstup:except=-FRPBLGTS}` ([Send on the first key up](#/ref/punctuation/send-on-the-first-key-up)). Hold the modifier keys and `LGTS` on the right hand, tap characters on the left: each tap is one shortcut. Hold Super + `LGTS`, tap `1`, `2`, `3` ([[RAOPLGTS]], [[WAOPLGTS]], [[WRAOPLGTS]]).

**Exempt keys.** The exception `-FRPBLGTS` lists every right-hand key of the held base (the modifiers `F` `R` `P` `B` and the ender `L` `G` `T` `S`; `D` and `Z` are never in a chord here). The left-hand and vowel keys are not exempt: the first of them to come up sends the stroke. A chord with no left-hand key (`-FLGTS`) goes on its last key up. Needs a keymux build that reads `{:firstup:except=KEYS}`; plain Plover errors on the marker.

blocks.x: Modifier keys
Any of 15 non-empty combinations, in steno order `F R P B` before `LGTS`. Wrapping, innermost first: Shift, Alt, Super, Ctrl.
Modifiers alone are strokes: [[-FLGTS]] [[-RLGTS]] [[-BLGTS]] [[-PLGTS]] are Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Super; other combinations likewise.
The generating rule
Six parts, in order: left-hand consonants, `A`/`O`, `*` or `-`, `E`/`U`, modifier keys `F R P B`, ender `LGTS`. The first three groups select what is pressed:

blocks.x: Chords not in the tables are not strokes. 98 base chords times 15 modifier combinations = 1,470 strokes. One stroke per output: chords equivalent to another (an extra `T`, `E` or `U`) are not strokes.
Numbers and function keys

Strike `AO` with no `E`, `U` or star. The left hand's bottom row counts in binary: **`R`=1, `W`=2, `K`=4, `S`=8**, summed. Digits up to 9. Only the table's chords are strokes; an extra `T`, `H` or `P` is not.
Adding `T` and `P` makes the count a function key (F1 to F12; the count is the number the chord spells):
A count above 9 is not a digit; a function-key count of 0 or above 12 is not a stroke (there is no F0).
Symbols and special keys

A star switches the chord from letters and digits to this table. `A` and `O` select one of up to four variants: none, `A`, `O`, `A` and `O` together. `E`, `U` or `EU` as well makes no stroke. Only keys a US keyboard presses and keymux can send have a stroke: no Audio Play, Prev, Next or Stop, and no typographic symbols (`¬ ¡ × ÷ ¿ « » µ`). Strokes are shown with Ctrl (`F`); any other modifier combination substitutes.
Examples: [[K*FLGTS]] is Ctrl+`.`; [[TPW*FLGTS]] is Ctrl+`?`; [[KPWR*FPBLGTS]] is Ctrl+Super+Alt+Up (`{:firstup:except=-FRPBLGTS}{^}{#control(super(alt(up)))}{^}`).
